transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-02
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Omar Haddad (CSM) -- Marcus Reed (SableWorks), Alana Cho, Diego Ramos, Priya Patel

Auto Summary (auto gen, may be noisy):
- Reviewed sprint-2 bench results: P50/P95 latency and RPS vs baseline provider (Lexigen).
- Identified two hotspots: KV cache misses on long-context prompts and suboptimal batching config for peak bursts.
- Agreed on routing threshold for fallback to smaller quantized variant and a short dedicated slot for head-to-head load test next week.
- Next: Redwood to share trimmed CSV, routing playbook; SableWorks to share traffic shape and auth sample.

Topics:
- Latency P50/P95 deltas, per-model throughput, batch size impact, quantization tradeoffs, private VPC wiring (note mis-transcribe: privet wiring), security doc request.

Action items (quick list):
- Send CSV + notes (Jordan)
- Routing playbook (Priya)
- Traffic sample + auth header (Alana)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: all right good afternoon everyone uh thanks for carving time we have about an hour, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, priya's with me from SE, omar from CS. How's everyone doing?
[00:18] Marcus Reed: good thanks we're, yeah busy but good. Diego on mute for now.
[00:22] Priya Nair: quick agenda — confirm results from sprint two, triage the two regressions we saw, and agree next steps for the head-to-head load. sound good?
[00:32] Alana Cho: yep that's fine. we also wanted to show a short trace where we saw p95 jumps during our 1k rps burst.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: perfect, Marcus do you want to kick off with the numbers you pulled into the sheet?
[00:45] Marcus Reed: sure, uh so the CSV we uploaded has runs A,B,C, i pulled p50 and p95, for typical prompt (avg tokens 240) the baseline provider lexigen p50 was 110ms and p95 320ms. Redwood during our standard run p50 120ms p95 400ms — so delta at p95 is ~80ms. throughput wise at steady state baseline plateaued at 450 rps, redwood hit 520 rps with batching but with the burst test we saw tail spikes.
[01:18] Priya Nair: yeah to call out — the extra headroom at steady state is the batching / continuous batching in the runtime, but the p95 spike is what we need to triage. we correlated those to KV cache misses when the prompt had long prefix and multiple tool calls, also some worker requeueing during the burst.
[01:36] Diego Ramos: just to be clear, when you say KV cache miss, is that per-request cold start of kv or something else?
[01:42] Priya Nair: good q. it's primarily the KV cache being invalidated due to differing prompt keys from our sampling — so the runtime couldn't reuse the kv entries and that forces extra compute per token. also some of our kernels go to slower path for sequences >2k which affects tail. transcription note: "kernels" got auto changed to "carnels" in our internal parser sometimes.
[02:06] Marcus Reed: got it. we also saw auth handshake jitter in one run — likely our test harness hitting retries (we use short lived jwt). Alana we'll drop the auth header sample.
[02:16] Alana Cho: yes i'll send the sample token and the sha header, you'll see our traffic shape attached.
[02:22] Jordan Lee: excellent. quick question on the baseline comparison — do you have the Lexigen run logs for the exact traffic shape? you mentioned 1k burst — was that identical?
[02:30] Marcus Reed: we tried to mirror it; slight diff, lexigen test used a smoother ramp, ours had microbursts every 30s. i flagged that in the CSV.
[02:38] Priya Nair: ok that explains some delta. for the next head-to-head we should align ramp and microburst cadence.
[02:44] Diego Ramos: another note: latency SLA for our product is p95 <350ms, so at p95 400ms it's just outside our acceptable window.
[02:52] Jordan Lee: understood, we should be able to close that with two levers: tighten batching policy for bursts and enable prefix caching on your side for repeated system prompts, plus a temporary quantized variant with faster kernels for fallback.
[03:08] Marcus Reed: about the quantized variant — any quality regressions we should watch for? we can't tolerate hallucination increase.
[03:14] Priya Nair: great question. our quantize-8 profile for that model historically shows <1% delta on eval set for QA-like prompts; i'll attach the eval matrix. but we will only route to it when latency threshold breached and we also keep a sample of outputs for real-time QA. transcription artifact: "quantize" sometimes shows up as "quant eyes" in the transcript.
[03:34] Diego Ramos: ok how about dedicated slot time — you mentioned a short dedicated slot for the head-to-head?
[03:39] Jordan Lee: yes, we can reserve a dedicated slot (2 x A100 equivalent) for a 2 hour window to reproduce the burst and run a controlled handoff. that's a temporary reserved capacity, we'll scope cost in the runbook.
[03:52] Marcus Reed: sounds good. can we also get a quick run where caching is disabled to measure baseline compute only?
[03:58] Priya Nair: yes we can toggle cache on/off, that's part of the experiments. we'll include three runs: full cache, no cache, and fallback quantized.
[04:07] Alana Cho: question on VPC — we need to confirm routing via private link, and also the KMS key for encryption at rest. your doc earlier referenced KMS binding but i couldn't find the exact header examples.
[04:19] Omar Haddad: right — we'll share the security snapshot and the KMS sample. small caveat: if you're on prem you may need HSM for some regulations, we support KMS/HSM integrations though.
[04:30] Diego Ramos: that is important for compliance. transcription note: "H-S-M" got expanded oddly in the quick notes.
[04:36] Jordan Lee: i'll attach SOC2 excerpt and the VPC wiring diagram and we'll flag the HSM path.
[04:42] Marcus Reed: thanks. back to the numbers, do you have any quick theories for the requeueing during the burst?
[04:48] Priya Nair: requeue is usually scheduler backpressure — when worker kernel time spikes some requests are requeued to avoid head-of-line blocking. tuning the scheduling window and max batch size helped in our internal runs. for your traffic microbursts i'd recommend lowering max batch size from 64 to 32 and a more aggressive max wait time like 6ms for microburst-sensitive SLA.
[05:14] Alana Cho: that aligns with what we saw when we tried small batch runs earlier. but i worry about throughput loss. any data on throughput delta if we lower max batch?
[05:22] Priya Nair: expected steady throughput might drop ~6-8% at plateau but p95 improves significantly. since your plateau already beat baseline, it's a reasonable trade for meeting SLA. we'll include a throughput vs batch table in the runbook.
[05:36] Marcus Reed: can you also include per-token cost delta? procurement cares about unit economics.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: yes we will provide token-level cost for each experiment (full cache, no cache, quantized fallback) and a recommended default.
[05:47] Diego Ramos: ok timeline — what are next steps to get the head-to-head scheduled?
[05:52] Jordan Lee: actions — Jordan send CSV and annotated runbook by Fri 2/4, Priya to draft routing playbook and fallback thresholds by Mon 2/5, Alana to share traffic shape + JWT sample by Thu 2/3. We target the dedicated slot test next Tue 2/9 18:00 UTC (10am PT) pending your sign-off.
[06:12] Marcus Reed: that day/time works for us tentatively.
[06:16] Priya Nair: one more thing — during the test we'll stream a small sample of outputs to your qa channel so you can monitor quality. we'll keep retention short and anonymized.
[06:26] Priya Patel: quick question, will logs include token-level traces or just aggregate metrics?
[06:30] Omar Haddad: aggregate metrics plus optional pseudo-token traces we scrub personally identifiable info out. full token traces require additional consents.
[06:40] Diego Ramos: fine. any blockers to the plan?
[06:43] Marcus Reed: none on our side, just need the CSV and playbook.
[06:47] Jordan Lee: perfect. we'll follow up in email with attachments. thanks everyone.
[06:52] Diego Ramos: thanks all.

End of transcript.
